candidate_names: Rio Vila Nova ou Anauerapucu (IBGE printed reach alias)
records.region: Amapá, Brazil; Vila Nova corridor between the Porto Grande/Mazagão interior and Santana/Mazagão lower waters.
records.candidate_name_role: Directly supported upper, middle and lower component identity, provisionally representative only; not a completed identity for the entire selected group.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected lower-fragment passage south of Camaipi/Nossa Senhora da Conceição swings west of the depicted Vila Nova trunk, then runs east to rejoin near Anauerapucu. The readable IBGE and independent CPRM originals do not establish a continuous watercourse for this whole selected bypass. This is an ordinary through-link gap, not an exact-bank/vertex test or merely an absent name.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Rio Vila Nova is a provisional component/system candidate; IBGE also prints the reach alias Rio Vila Nova ou Anauerapucu. The selected lower-fragment western bypass south of Camaipi remains unestablished before the route rejoins near Anauerapucu. The actual terminal lies in lower Vila Nova, upstream of the broader Matapi–Amazonas receiving-channel complex.
records.completion_scope: Rio Vila Nova is a provisional component/system candidate; IBGE also prints the reach alias Rio Vila Nova ou Anauerapucu. The selected lower-fragment western bypass south of Camaipi remains unestablished before the route rejoins near Anauerapucu. The actual terminal lies in lower Vila Nova, upstream of the broader Matapi–Amazonas receiving-channel complex. The record remains one primary source-material-pending classification; source failures are details, not an additional pending count.
records.supported_name_scope: The IBGE original prints Rio Vila Nova ou Anauerapucu on the upper and lower trunk; CPRM prints Rio Vila Nova. These observations do not rename Rio Piaçacá, Rio Camaipi do Vila Nova, Rio Matapi, the distinct Anauerapucu-side watercourses, or the Amazonas receiving channels.

component_scope_limits: The unresolved westward lower-fragment passage cannot be replaced by the readily named nearby Vila Nova trunk merely because both lie in the same basin.

IBGE’s Rio Vila Nova ou Anauerapucu label is recorded at its printed reach scope. It does not resolve every local use of Anauerapucu or make the separate locality/side-watercourse labels global synonyms.
The selected terminal is lower-river geography. The stored sea classification is not confirmed as an actual open-ocean endpoint.
Historical cartography and the2015/2023 locality publications are not evidence of current discharge, flood/ebb extent, channel operations, water levels or a formal naming registry.

records.region: Southwestern Victoria Island, Arctic Canada; Mount Bumpus interior lake country, Tassijuak lake/river corridor and Clouston Bay.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected northern lake succession, transfer south/west from the eastern large lake, and subsequent north-to-south passage into the Tassijuak lake approach are not established as continuous selected connections in the readable historical maps. Mapped alternative outlets and nearby lake membership cannot supply those links.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selection opens in the Mount Bumpus lake country, turns east and northeast, descends along both sides of the Read Island/Banning Lake sheet join, turns west through the Tassijuak lake and river corridor, and ends at Clouston Bay. Source map coverage of this extent is complete; positive correspondence of every actual selected transfer is not.
records.completion_scope: Both complete original maps were acquired serially and the entire selected extent, including all32 constituent sublines, was considered using source-only corridor windows. Required northern, eastern and southern inland transfers remain materially unestablished. This is one material-pending result, not completed representative identity, completed name-scope hold, or an added access-pending record.
records.supported_name_scope: Tassijuak River is directly printed on the selected southern westward river corridor. Tassijuak Lake is a separately supported lake component. Unresolved selected inland connections prevent promotion to a completed representative identity; no uniform whole-route name is assigned.

component_scope_limits: No name or map proximity repairs an unresolved selected connection.
No source, mouth or legal name boundary is assigned to an exact modeled vertex.
No source is required to name every creek; the outstanding issue is actual selected through-links.
The recorded historical fishery and seasonality prose is not current fisheries or navigation advice.

records.region: Northern Greenland, southern Mylius-Erichsen Land and the Femte Maj Sø–Jyske Ås–Hagen Fjord setting.
records.candidate_name_role: No representative natural-river identity established. Femte Maj Sø, Mylius-Erichsen Land, Jyske Ås and Hagen Fjord are distinct geographic context labels only.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Both original maps together expose every selected part, including the opening south of 81°N, bedrock/local-ice transitions, Femte Maj Sø lake-side setting, Quaternary-covered valley, northern Jyske Ås passage and actual Hagen Fjord ending. They do not establish one representative named natural river across this modeled sequence.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected object opens south of 81°N in southern Mylius-Erichsen Land, runs east and then turns north and back west before passing northeast along the Femte Maj Sø lake/shore setting. It continues east across a valley-and-bedrock belt, turns north near the eastern local-ice/rock area, and continues through the Jyske Ås setting to Hagen Fjord. The source cartography contains distinct exposed-rock, ice, lake-water, Quaternary-cover and fjord areas. Its labels are not conflated into a river name.
records.completion_scope: The opening and southern interval are covered by the national 1995 original. The regional 1986 original begins at 81°N, overlaps the incoming northern part and covers the remainder of the selected sequence, including every small stored part in the eastward corridor, the eastern bend, northward continuation and actual terminal. Source graticules, legend and imprint were read. There is no substantial unviewed interval at ordinary source scale. Exact shore vertices, lake-inlet/outlet positions, current local-ice limits and present hydraulic continuity are not claimed.

component_scope_limits: Femte Maj Sø is a mapped lake name, Hagen Fjord a fjord name, and Jyske Ås and Mylius-Erichsen Land landform/regional labels. None names the whole selected river group.
The modeled passage includes local ice/rock and lake-side settings. Neither map proves a surveyed, continuous river along all selected parts or a hydraulic connection through lake/ice sections.

The national map’s surface contours, ice-thickness isopachs, sub-ice bedrock contours and aeromagnetic lineaments are distinct from river evidence. Regional geological contacts and dykes are likewise not watercourse proof.
Historical map epochs do not establish contemporary drainage, lake level, glacier extent or exact shore position.
A null candidate means this research did not establish the name; it does not assert that no local or official name exists.

records.region: Central Mexico; Tlaxcala–Hidalgo–northern Valley of Mexico drainage and El Caracol setting.
records.candidate_name_role: No representative name is established for the complete selected San Fernando–San Antonio Atocha–Apan/Tepeapulco–Tizayuca–Zumpango–El Caracol corridor. Waterbody names and separately mapped stream names below are bounded component/context observations, not an assertion that any names the entire selection.
records.material_pending_reason: The chosen San Fernando–Bernales–Atocha transfers, the Atocha-to-northern-plain connection, intermediate infrastructure and lake-side exchanges, and the final El Caracol-area receiving link remain unestablished. These are actual route connections, not a demand for a name on every stream or exact bank/vertex agreement.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected San Fernando–San Antonio Atocha–Tepeapulco–Tizayuca–Zumpango–El Caracol corridor crosses intermittent-channel, lake, aqueduct and managed-drainage settings. Original maps and engineering prose distinguish those components but do not establish the selected transfers or final receiving link; no whole-system name is assigned.
records.completion_scope: Original state cartography was read across the selected opening, all intermediate selected intervals and the actual southern ending, with municipal hydrographic maps at the opening, Tlanalapa join and Zumpango turn. The maps contain intermittent channels, reservoirs/lakes, aqueducts and managed urban drainage. Readable map coverage is not complete positive through-link correspondence: the particular selected transfers between these elements remain materially unestablished. The primary result is source-material pending, not a completed naming-scope hold. No source or geometry substitution was made.
records.supported_name_scope: No representative name is established for the complete selected San Fernando–San Antonio Atocha–Apan/Tepeapulco–Tizayuca–Zumpango–El Caracol corridor. Waterbody names and separately mapped stream names below are bounded component/context observations, not an assertion that any names the entire selection.

component_scope_limits: The selected San Fernando–Bernales–Atocha passage combines intermittent channels, impounded waters and mapped aqueduct infrastructure without positive evidence for each chosen transfer.
The west-Atocha exit and northward plain passage through Zotoluca, Chimalpa Tlalayote, Acopinalco and Irolo remain a material connection gap.
The middle plain’s branch and infrastructure transitions, the selected Zumpango lake-side exchange and the final El Caracol-area receiving link are not fully established.

A naturally closed basin, the stored endorheic designation, a connected model line, a regional basin name and a nearby hydrographic label do not establish actual present flow, engineered transfer or one representative river identity.

The maps are generalized historical compilations. No current water level, discharge, operating status, exact bank, surveyed source, naming-transition vertex or formal registry entry has been verified.
El Jihuingo, Las Avenidas de Pachuca, waterbody names and named drainage works have their own bounded scopes; they are not interchangeable whole-selection names.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
